item.title: The Casimir on the $K$-fixed tensor square of the minimal representation of $G_{2(2)}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the quadratic Casimir on the $K$-fixed subspace of the Hilbert tensor square of the unitary minimal representation of the split real group $G_{2(2)}$. In an explicit algebraic basis of invariant tensors, the Casimir acts by a three-term recurrence. Normalizing this basis yields a symmetric Jacobi operator whose self-adjoint realization is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $-\frac92-8x^2$ in a Wilson-polynomial model with parameters $(\frac34,\frac34,\frac7{12},\frac{11}{12})$. We give the normalized spectral density and the unitary transform. The resulting spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, equals $(-\infty,-\frac92]$, and has scalar spectral multiplicity one.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Yuan

item.title: Local Converse Theorems for $k$-Middle Supercuspidal Representations of $p$-adic $\text{GL}(kn)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\text{F}$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero with residual characteristic $p$. In this paper, we study local converse theorems for $k$-middle supercuspidal representations of $\text{GL}(kn, \text{F})$ via explicit computations of twisted gamma factors on the Galois side, under the assumptions $p \nmid kn$ and $q_{\text{F}}>(k-1)^2$. Our results provide further evidence for a conjecture of the third-named author and Stevens on depth bounds for the twisting representations in the local converse theorem. For odd $k \ge 3$, we obtain infinitely many families of supercuspidal representations for which the bound $\left\lfloor \frac{kn}{2} \right\rfloor$ in the local converse theorem is not sharp.
item.dc:creator: Moshe Adrian, Michael Horzepa, David C. Luo

item.title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.25101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra. As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Jun Hu, Andrew Mathas, Lei Shi, Ben Webster

item.title: Non-canonical Oscillator Representations of Orthogonal Lie Algebras and Pfaffian Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.25157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Associated varieties are fundamental geometric invariants in the study of infinite-dimensional representations of semisimple Lie algebras. Luo and Xu (2013) constructed a large family of infinite-dimensional irreducible representations of orthogonal Lie algebras by applying Fourier transforms to the natural oscillator representations. In this paper, we prove that the associated varieties of these irreducible representations are isomorphic to explicitly described coordinate linear sections of Pfaffian varieties. The modules are realized as spaces of polynomial solutions of transformed Laplace equations. We construct filtrations from weighted polynomial degrees and determine the annihilator ideals of the corresponding associated graded modules. The defining equations consist of linear coordinate equations, minors and quadratic Pfaffian relations. The even and odd orthogonal Lie algebras are treated separately. The associated varieties are viewed as reduced affine schemes over a field of characteristic zero. In each irreducible family with fixed Fourier parameters, the associated variety is independent of the grading parameter. When the two Fourier parameters coincide, the projectivizations in the even case are Grassmannians.
item.dc:creator: Hengjia Zhang

item.title: Generalized symmetric pairs, Lie superalgebras, Dirac operators and Kostant constants
item.description: arXiv:2610.25226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a geometric construction of contragredient Lie superalgebras, with the exceptions of $A(m,n)$ $(m,n>0)$ and $G(3)$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an order 4 automorphism $\sigma$, the eigenspace decomposition being $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)$. When $\mathfrak{g}(i)$ admits a $\mathfrak{g}(1)$-invariant symplectic structure, $(\mathfrak{g},\sigma)$ is called a \emph{generalized symmetric pair with symplectic subspace}. In this paper, we classify all such pairs and construct a natural Lie superalgebra structure on $L= L_{\bar{0}}+L_{\bar{1}}$ with $L_{\bar{0}}=\mathfrak{g}(1)$ and $L_{\bar{1}}=\mathfrak{g}(i)$. Furthermore, we investigate the constants arising from the squares of two distinct Dirac operators: $D$ for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}^{\sigma^2}+\mathfrak{g}^{-\sigma^2}$, and $D_s$ for $L=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)$. We prove that the constant $C$ in $D^2$ admits a remarkable factorization \[C=J^*(\Omega_{L_{\bar{0}}})\cdot\dim L_{\bar{1}}\cdot h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}},\] where $h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}}$ is the signed dual Coxeter number of $L$ and $J^*(\Omega_{L_{\bar{0}}})$ is a mapped Casimir constant of its even part. This formula reveals an unexpected unification of symmetric space geometry and Lie superalgebra invariants. Finally, we prove that the Kostant constant $\mathrm{K_s} = \left.\Omega_{L_{\bar{0}}}\right|_{L_{\bar{1}}}=\frac{1}{2}$ is universal for all contragredient Lie superalgebras with non-degenerate Killing form, which implies that the constant $C_s$ in $D_s^2$ satisfies $C_s=\frac{1}{16}\dim L_{\bar{0}}$. We then establish a bijection between such superalgebras and solutions of the superadmissibility index equations $E_s^{I\!I} =\frac{1}{2}, E_s^I = \frac{1}{2}$, recovering the classification from an invariant-theoretic perspective.
item.dc:creator: Mingjing Zhang, Fuhai Zhu

item.title: Cellular bases of mirabolic Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the mirabolic Hecke algebra $\mathscr{H}_{n,R}(q)$ over a commutative ring $R$ is cellular by constructing explicit cellular bases. When $R=\mathbb{K}$ is a field, we also establish a Morita equivalence between $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$ and a direct sum of Hecke algebras associated with symmetric groups. As applications, we classify the irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules and obtain a semisimplicity criterion. Finally, when $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}(q)$, we show that the cell modules arising from one of our cellular bases coincide with Siegel's irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Yan Liu Jinkui Wan, Xirui Yu

item.title: The associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$, one can associate a graded algebra (denoted by $\mathrm{gr}(A)$) with the radical filtration of $A$. An interesting question is to compare the representation theories of $A$ and $\mathrm{gr}(A)$. When $A$ is a Brauer graph algebra with defining Brauer graph $\Gamma$, we have described the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ in terms of the information of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we describe the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ when $A$ is a biserial fractional Brauer graph algebra - a notion that properly generalizes a Brauer graph algebra - in terms of the information of the defining biserial fractional Brauer graph $\Gamma$ of $A$.
item.dc:creator: Jing Guo, Nengqun Li, Yuming Liu

item.title: Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type
item.description: arXiv:2610.25312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Asashiba

item.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.25597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation \`{a} la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki

item.title: Quantum symmetric spaces at roots of 1
item.description: arXiv:2610.25624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the integral form of quantized coordinate algebras of symmetric spaces and its specializations at roots of unity. Our main tool is an integral localization, whose classical specialization recovers the open Borel orbit in the symmetric space. At a suitable odd root of unity, we prove that the quantum symmetric space is a finite projective module over its Frobenius center, which is canonically isomorphic to the classical coordinate algebra of the symmetric space. We show that the fibre algebras are isomorphic along each double Bruhat cell of the symmetric space. We determine the PI degree and propose a conjectural dimension formula for irreducible modules. In the simply connected case, we introduce a framed Kac-Moody data, which leads to a description of fibre algebras of quantum symmetric spaces via those of quantum Schubert cells.
item.dc:creator: Jinfeng Song, Weinan Zhang

item.title: Cohomology and Representation Theory for Lie Superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper the authors describe two general frameworks for studying algebraic supergroup and Lie superalgebra representations. These encompass the well-known rational representations for a reductive algebraic group and the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}$ for semisimple Lie algebras. Many of the important developments will be surveyed and a blueprint for these new approaches will be provided. The existence of odd elements simply add an additional layer of difficulty. The authors prove that the calculation of the sheaf cohomology in the super setting for the rational category is equivalent to understanding the Lie superalgebra cohomology. This generalizes the well-known fact that the classical Bott-Borel-Weil theorem is equivalent to Kostant's theorem. Furthermore, for the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}^{\mathfrak p}$ where ${\mathfrak p}$ is a principal parabolic, the authors show that the characters of simple modules can be obtained by looking at natural generalizations of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials given by extensions between simple modules and costandard modules arising from the underlying costandardly stratified category.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Grantcharov, Daniel K. Nakano

item.title: Lusztig's asymptotic algebra and a cell factorisation for the second lowest two-sided cell in type $\tilde{B}_n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine Lusztig's asymptotic algebra for the second lowest two-sided cell~$\Delta_1$ in the equal parameter extended affine Weyl group $\tilde{\mathsf{B}}_n$ for all $n\geq 2$, realising it as a full matrix algebra over the representation ring of $\mathsf{Sp}_{2n-2}(\CC)\times C_2$ with $C_2$ the group of order~$2$. Our result is an explicit isomorphism of based rings, determining the image of each basis element $\mathsf{t}_w$ of the asymptotic algebra. As a consequence we verify that Lusztig's original conjecture from 1989 on the structure of the asymptotic algebra holds for this cell. A key ingredient in our proof is a refinement of Shi's description of~$\Delta_1$, giving an explicit parametrisation of the elements of this cell (a \textit{cell factorisation}). This cell factorisation simultaneously describes all intersections of left and right cells, with uniqueness and length-additivity of expressions. Applications include a classification of the involutions in $\Delta_1$, and a calculation of the length generating functions for $\Delta_1$ and the right cells in~$\Delta_1$.
item.dc:creator: James Parkinson

item.title: Brauer and iquantum categorification
item.description: arXiv:2610.25922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that locally finite Abelian module categories over the affine Brauer category are the same thing as locally finite Abelian 2-representations of a certain 2-iquantum group satisfying some additional nilpotency and finiteness properties. Our results are valid over algebraically closed fields of characteristic other than 2 and for arbitrary spectra. This extends recent work of Gao, Rui and Song, who treated characteristic 0 with half-integral spectrum. The relevant Satake diagrams are of quasi-split type AIII and of diagonal type A, including affine types in positive characteristic. The key step in our approach identifies the affine Brauer category with a topologically dense monoidal subcategory of a completion of the 2-iquantum group. As an application, we show that deformed cyclotomic quotients on the two sides are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Brundan, Alistair Savage, Ben Webster

item.title: Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thi\'ery, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thi\'ery, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko

item.title: Counting Irreducible Components of the Semistable Global Nilpotent Cone
item.description: arXiv:2610.26085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss various methods for parametrizing and counting irreducible components of the global nilpotent cone of semistable $G$-Higgs bundles on a smooth complex curve. By restricting our study to the case of generically regular components following previous work of Faergeman and Raskin, we obtain explicit counts of semistable generically regular irreducible components for $G = \mathrm{SL}_n$, and give the first examples of such counts outside type A. These numbers are obtained by counting points in some natural polytopes associated to $G$, but our method requires a finer analysis in cases where the center of the group $G$ is disconnected.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Seroux

item.title: Decomposing the Action of Macdonald Operators for Classical Types
item.description: arXiv:2610.26389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Macdonald operators associated to classical root systems of types $B_N$, $C_N$, and $D_N$. We provide explicit formulas for decomposing the cumulative action of these operators as the sum of the actions of lower-rank operators and auxiliary operators. We also discuss the same idea in the elliptic case, also known as Ruijsenaars operators, and show that under the trigonometric limit, the identity reduces to type-$A_N$ decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: Socle formulas for rigid irreducible components of Lusztig's nilpotent varieties in type $A$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field. For any irreducible component $C$ of a nilpotent variety of type $A$ let $\pi(C)$ be the irreducible representation of a general linear group over $F$ attached to it. We show that if the multisegment of $C$ is multiplicity free, $C$ is rigid if and only if $\pi(C)$ is $\square$-irreducible. In this case, \[ \pi(C*D)=soc\bigl(\pi(C)\times\pi(D)\bigr),\qquad \pi(D*C)=soc\bigl(\pi(D)\times\pi(C)\bigr) \] for every irreducible component $D$, where $*$ is the binary operation defined by Aizenbud and Lapid, in accordance with a conjecture of Lapid and M\'inguez. We also give a computer-assisted example in $A_7$ of a non-simple rigid module $z\ne0$ which does not admit a proper rigid submodule $y\ne0$ such that $Ext_\Pi^1(z,z/y)=0$, answering negatively a question of Aizenbud and Lapid.
item.dc:creator: Erez Lapid, Alberto M\'{\i}nguez

item.title: Ramanujan Conjecture and Riemann Hypothesis for the unitary groups over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.23985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish generic local and global Langlands functoriality, namely stable base change, for the unitary groups in characteristic $p$. Main applications are the Ramanujan Conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis for extended Langlands-Shahidi $L$-functions of the unitary groups over function fields.
item.dc:creator: Luis Alberto Lomel\'i

item.title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a notion of a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on a poset, and conjecture the existence of such an action is equivalent to the existence of a symmetric chain decomposition of that poset. We explain the intuition behind the conjecture, go through a number of explicit examples, and prove some special cases and relaxations of the conjecture. Then we explain a computational experiment where we tested the conjecture on millions of randomly constructed rank-symmetric, rank-unimodal, and strongly Sperner posets.
item.dc:creator: Nate Harman, Rylan Rosas, Charles Troutman III, Chris Wu

item.title: Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Pl\"ucker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Pl\"ucker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.
item.dc:creator: Li Cai, Haoran Liu, Mingyu Yang, Wenyan Yang

item.title: The big cactus group, invariant tensors, and rectangular tableaux
item.description: arXiv:2610.24842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The cactus group acts on tensor products of crystals and, through Bender--Knuth involutions, on semistandard Young tableaux. We show that the big cactus group $J'_n=\pi_1^{\mathfrak S_n}(\overline M_{0,n}(\mathbb R))$, $n\ge3$, is obtained from the cactus group by imposing $n-1$ Dynkin-reversal relations, which say that conjugation by the full reversal acts on the Bender--Knuth generators by the Dynkin diagram automorphism; the quotient map is induced by forgetting the distinguished marked point. We give a second presentation, in which these relations are replaced by the requirement that every reduced word for the longest element of $\mathfrak S_n$ adapted to an orientation of $A_{n-1}$ represents the full reversal. These relations also hold on rectangular tableaux, where every adapted reduced word therefore acts as evacuation, and on invariant tensors: for finite normal crystals of any complex semisimple Lie algebra, the cactus action on invariants factors through $J'_n$. We prove the latter combinatorially in type $A$ and in general via Gaudin eigenline coverings. Haiman's promotion relation follows from a single adapted-word relation, but for $n\ge4$ it is strictly weaker than the whole family.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Frieden, Pavlo Pylyavskyy, Leonid Rybnikov

item.title: On the classification of threefold flops
item.description: arXiv:2610.24864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that possibly singular threefold flopping contractions are completely classified by their associated derived contraction algebras, considered up to derived Morita equivalence; in contrast to the smooth case the extra derived structure is necessary in general. This extends previous work of the author on simple flops, and follows from a more general theorem about isolated hypersurface singularities. The key new input is to show that derived localisation at a Hochschild class is Morita invariant; this result raises some interesting questions related to the classification of recollements. We also show that derived contraction algebras admit a deformation-theoretic interpretation in families in a general setting that encompasses threefold flops, flips, and divisor-to-curve contractions.
item.dc:creator: Matt Booth

item.title: Classification of twisted Yangians as coideal subalgebras of Yangians
item.description: arXiv:2610.25003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an involution $\omega$. We classify the homogeneous right coideal subalgebras of the Yangian of $\mathfrak g$ whose classical limit is the enveloping algebra of the twisted current algebra, embedded in the standard way, without assuming any formula for the coaction. For nontrivial $\omega$, they form a family parametrized by a spectral parameter and an element of the center of the fixed-point subalgebra; for $\omega=\mathrm{id}$, only a spectral parameter occurs. All members of the family are isomorphic as graded algebras, through explicit isomorphisms. In particular, the twisted Yangians with a central correction introduced by Huang and Lu are coideal quantizations, and the $\imath$Yangian of quasi-split type $\mathsf A_{2n}$ is isomorphic to the traditional twisted Yangian studied by MacKay and by Belliard and Regelskis. The PBW property is proved uniformly from the classical affine Serre relations, without quantum defining relations. We also recover finite presentations in split and quasi-split types and verify the technical hypotheses of the quantum duality principle used by Lu, Wang, and Weekes.
item.dc:creator: Kang Lu

item.title: The 3-adic Steinberg block and a categorical 3-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the work of Johansson-Newton-Wang-Erickson on a categorical $p$-adic Langlands correspondence over $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ to $p = 3$ by recontextualizing their construction in the Steinberg case. We produce a novel, more categorical method of analyzing the properties of this construction without requiring an explicit algebraic presentation. As input to this argument, we also perform some new analysis of the representation theory of the $3$-adic Steinberg block of $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$, obtaining results complementing those of Pa\v{s}k\={u}nas.
item.dc:creator: CJ Dowd

item.title: Super Howe duality and rigidity of hybrid Fourier transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.25057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize the hybrid Fourier transform on the Schwartz--Grassmann space $\caS(\bbR^m)\otimes\Lambda_{2n}$ by operator intertwining relations. Using the bosonic oscillator Howe decomposition and the fermionic Lefschetz decomposition, we describe the action of the hybrid Fourier transform on both tensor factors. We show that first-order covariance with respect to coordinate multiplication and differentiation determines the transform up to a scalar. For $m,n\ge1$, we prove that covariance under all even quadratic operators, together with any one nonzero mixed quadratic operator, determines the linear span of the hybrid Fourier transform and its inverse. This rigidity result is obtained by computing the ordinary commutants of the even and full quadratic oscillator actions of $\fosp(4n|2m)$. After a degree-scaling change of normalization, we make the hybrid Fourier transform unitary with respect to the occupation number inner product, and factor it into a bosonic oscillator rotation and (up to a scalar phase) an $SU(2)$ rotation in the fermionic Lefschetz representation. For $m=1$ and $n\ge2$, we show that full even quadratic covariance together with the parity-preserving cubic relation for $qQ_f$ determines the unitary transform up to a global phase and a fermion-parity phase. Finally we calculate the unitary conjugation formulas for Hubbard--Holstein Hamiltonian for a hybrid continuous-variable and discrete-variable quantum system.
item.dc:creator: Jing-Song Huang, Yongzhi Luan, Yinuo Xue

item.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.25143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a theory on duality between groups and the categories of their representations, by providing an abstract characterization of such categories. The theory has two parallel formulations, each presenting a duality analogous to one of the two that were originally proposed by Grothendieck: the one between profinite groups and the abstract categories of their continuous representations on finite sets, and the other between affine group schemes over a field and the abstract categories of their finite-dimensional linear representations. In the present theory, groups and their representations are internal to a symmetric monoidal base category, with no finiteness condition imposed. The role of a fiber functor is played by a fiber point, an abstraction of the forgetful functor with its chosen adjoint. Over each base, a group determines the category of its representations equipped with the canonical fiber point, and a pointed abstract category determines the group that represents the presheaf of automorphisms of its chosen fiber point. These constructions yield mutually quasi-inverse equivalences of $(2,1)$-categories. By introducing change of base, we gather the dualities over individual bases into a single duality in each formulation. For a pointed abstract category, fiber points of the category are in perfect correspondence with torsors under the group associated to the chosen point. As an illustration of the theory, we reformulate the Galois theory of covering spaces for nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jaehyeok Lee, Jae-Suk Park

item.title: Superschemes and supermanifolds with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action
item.description: arXiv:2610.25564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that given an analytic supermanifold $X$ over a complete field on which the additive supergroup $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ of super-dimension $0|n$ acts freely (in an appropriate sense), the quotient $X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ exists as an analytic supermanifold, and the canonical morphism $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is an $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. A stronger version of this result is proven for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds, whereby $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is a trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. Previously, Polishchuk [18] established an algebro-geometric analogue, which proves that a superscheme $X$ with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action gives rise to a locally trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-torsor $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$. This result is proven here in an alternative, elementary way. To all of these, a Hopf-algebraic approach is effectively employed.
item.dc:creator: Akira Masuoka, Takuya Oe

item.title: Principal bundles in supersymmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.25811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Akira Masuoka

item.title: Flip classes and elementary expansions of vertical-strip LLT polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.26294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: After the substitution $q\mapsto q+1$, vertical-strip LLT polynomials are weighted sums of strict $P$-partition generating functions indexed by orientations of decorated unit-interval graphs, with weight $q^{\mathrm{asc}(\theta)}$. A flip moves an ascending edge across a triangle while keeping its long edge. We show that the sum over every flip class is elementary-positive: it equals the sum of the elementary symmetric functions given by the highest reachable vertices of its orientations. This answers Hwang's question on the Schur positivity of LLT flip-class sums, and it holds for circular unit-interval graphs as well. Summing over classes gives a new proof of the elementary expansion of Alexandersson and Sulzgruber, and its circular analog, which was open. We also obtain a flip-class refinement of the elementary expansion of LLT cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Per Alexandersson, Lilan Dai

item.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.26613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=w\lambda$ for real or octonion $\lambda$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(w\lambda_1)\lambda_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $\lambda_2\lambda_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Grigorian

item.title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.26774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $\kappa$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $\kappa$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives. The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures. Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.
item.dc:creator: Prakash Belkale, Najmuddin Fakhruddin

item.title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions over number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.26835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,\eta)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $\mu_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(\zeta_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].
item.dc:creator: Baiying Liu

item.title: Affine highest weight structures on module categories over quiver Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2412.12903v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the category of finitely generated graded modules over the quiver Hecke algebra of arbitrary type admits numerous stratifications in the sense of Kleshchev. A direct consequence is that the full subcategory corresponding to the quantum unipotent subgroup associated with any Weyl group element is an affine highest weight category. Our results significantly generalize earlier works by Kato, Brundan, Kleshchev, McNamara and Muth. The key ingredient is a realization of standard modules via determinantial modules. We utilize the technique of R-matrices to study these standard modules.
item.dc:creator: Haruto Murata

item.title: On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2502.10655v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies rational functions $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha(q)$, which depend on a positive element $\alpha$ of the root lattice of a root system. These functions arise as Shapovalov pairings of Whittaker vectors in Verma modules of highest weight $-\rho$ for quantum groups and as Hilbert series of Zastava spaces, and are related to the Toda system. They are specializations of multivariate functions more commonly studied in the literature. We investigate the denominator of these rational functions and give an explicit combinatorial formula for the numerator in type A. We also propose a conjectural realization of the numerator as the Poincar\'e polynomial of a smooth variety in type A.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Labelle

item.title: On certain Lagrangian subvarieties in minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities
item.description: arXiv:2504.08717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kleinian singularities are quotients of $\mathbb{C}^2$ by finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$. They are in bijection with the simply-laced Dynkin diagrams via the McKay correspondence. Anti-Poisson involutions and their fixed point loci appear naturally in the classification of irreducible Harish-Chandra modules over Kleinian singularities. There are three goals of this paper. The first is to classify anti-Poisson involutions of Kleinian singularities up to conjugation by graded Poisson automorphisms. The second is to describe the scheme-theoretic fixed point loci of Kleinian singularities under anti-Poisson involutions. The third and main goal is to describe the scheme-theoretic preimages of the fixed point loci under minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities. These preimages are singular Lagrangian subvarieties in the minimal resolutions whose irreducible components are $\mathbb{P}^1$'s and $\mathbb{A}^1$'s. Additionally, we discuss the connections between anti-Poisson involutions and Lie algebra involutions.
item.dc:creator: Mengwei Hu

item.title: The truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator
item.description: arXiv:2506.23599v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator between parabolically induced representations. This generalizes the symbol map, which is defined for the case of abelian nilpotent radicals, to the non-abelian setting. The inverse of the truncated symbol map enables one to develop a recipe for the F-method for any nilpotent radical. As an application, we classify and construct differential intertwining operators on the full flag variety $SL(3,\mathbb{R})/B$ and homomorphisms between Verma modules. It turned out that, surprisingly, Cayley continuants appeared in the coefficients of one of the five families of operators that we constructed. At the end of the paper, factorization identities for the differential operators and homomorphisms are also classified. Binary Krawtchouk polynomials play a key role in the proof.
item.dc:creator: Toshihisa Kubo, V\'ictor P\'erez-Vald\'es

item.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2509.17001v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Ullah

item.title: Brion atoms for classical types
item.description: arXiv:2512.19034v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a classical group defined over the complex numbers with a Borel subgroup $B$. Choose a holomorphic involution of $G$ and let $K$ be its set of fixed points. The group $K$ acts on the flag variety $G/B$ with finitely many orbits and Brion has derived a general formula for the cohomology classes of the corresponding orbit closures as linear combinations of Schubert classes. This article provides a uniform description of the sets of Weyl group elements (which we refer to as Brion atoms) that index the terms in this formula. We also include some applications of our classifications, including a refinement of Brion's cohomology formula.
item.dc:creator: Eric Marberg

item.title: Schur--Weyl duality for diagonalizing a Markov chain on the hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2512.23285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show how the tools of modern algebraic combinatorics -- representation theory, Murphy elements, and particularly Schur--Weyl duality -- can be used to give an explicit orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions for a "curiously slowly mixing Markov chain" on the space of binary $n$-tuples. The basis is used to give sharp rates of convergence to stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Persi Diaconis, Andrew Lin, Arun Ram

item.title: Koszul Duality for Quadratic Monomial Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.20177v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a quadratic monomial algebra and let \(\Lambda^{!}\) denote its Koszul dual. We study finitely presented and finitely copresented graded modules over \(\Lambda\) and \(\Lambda^{!}\), and use this structure to obtain explicit forms of derived and singular Koszul duality. We prove that quadratic monomial algebras are both graded coherent and graded cocoherent. Applying this to the Koszul dual \(\Lambda^{!}\), which is again quadratic monomial, we show that finitely presented and finitely copresented graded \(\Lambda^{!}\)-modules coincide with perfect and coperfect modules, respectively. It follows that the corresponding tails and cotails categories are hereditary abelian categories, and their objects are described in terms of linear and colinear modules. We also prove that quadratic monomial algebras are absolutely Koszul and have global linearity defect at most two. Consequently, finite-dimensional graded \(\Lambda\)-modules have rational Poincar\'e series, while finitely presented and finitely copresented graded \(\Lambda^{!}\)-modules have rational Hilbert series. As applications, we refine graded and ungraded derived Koszul dualities, singular Koszul dualities, and Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand correspondences for quadratic monomial algebras. We further describe the induced nonstandard \(t\)-structures on bounded derived and singularity categories and derive bounds for the finitistic dimension of \(\Lambda\) in terms of finite paths in the Koszul dual algebra.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Bouhada

item.title: M\"obius functions for pseudo-Levi subgroups in finite general linear and symplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.12522v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we compute the M\"obius function on the poset of pseudo-Levi subgroups containing a fixed maximal torus of two families of finite groups, $GL_n(q)$ and $Sp_{2n}(q)$, for some natural number $n$ and a prime power $q$, where $q>2n+1$. For the general linear group, we consider arbitrary tori, but for symplectic groups, we restrict to tori corresponding to the bipartitions of $n$ into odd integers. Also, we assume $q$ is even for the case of symplectic groups. The M\"obius function for the set of pseudo-Levi subgroups of a finite group $G$ is important for an explicit evaluation of the formula expressing the decomposition of tensor products of characters, as proved in Theorem 2 of the paper ''Multiplicity of characters of finite reductive groups and Drinfeld doubles'' [arXiv:2512.01432].
item.dc:creator: Aritra Kundu

item.title: Langlands Duality and Invariant Differential Operators: the Case SL(2n+1)
item.description: arXiv:2608.13400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently we started building a bridge between two cases of Langlands duality. The latter is one of the most influential topics in mathematical research. It has many different appearances and influential subtopics. Yet there is a topic that until now seems unrelated to the Langlands program. That is the topic of invariant differential operators. That is strange since both items are deeply rooted in Harish-Chandra's representation theory of semisimple Lie groups. We started with the case of the group ~$SL(2n)$. In the present paper we deal with the group $SL(2n+1)$. The two mentioned groups are similar, but their representation theories is rather different.
item.dc:creator: V. K. Dobrev

item.title: Morita equivalent blocks with an endotrivial source that are not globally isotypic
item.description: arXiv:2608.31083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(K,\mathcal{O},k)$ be a large enough $2$-modular system. We construct two nilpotent block algebras of finite groups which are isomorphic as $\mathcal{O}$-algebras and are Morita equivalent via a bimodule with an endotrivial source of $\mathcal{O}$-rank $3$, but which are not globally isotypic. Hence they are not $2$-permutation equivalent and not splendidly Rickard equivalent. These results separate Morita equivalences with endopermutation source from $p$-permutation equivalences and splendid Rickard equivalences, and also separate almost global isotypies from global isotypies.
item.dc:creator: Xin Huang

item.title: Singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type and standard eventually homological isomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.03365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We refine the definition of eventually homological isomorphisms so that it becomes more natural and fruitful. We introduce singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type which can be viewed as standard singular equivalences of different levels and are more convenient for reducing various homological conjectures and transferring homological properties. We develop the theories of singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type for $n\ge 2$ and standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories by giving their characterizations in terms of $\otimes$-(co)perfect complexes of bimodules, two constructions via opposite algebras and tensor product algebras, examples induced by homomorphisms of algebras and idempotents, and applications to the reduction of homological conjectures such as the finitistic dimension conjecture, Gorenstein symmetry conjecture and Auslander-Reiten conjecture, as well as to the preservation of homological properties such as Gorensteinness, the Fg condition, Happel's property and Han's property. Moreover, we show that essentially surjective standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories correspond to standard singular equivalences with canonical left adjoint.
item.dc:creator: Yang Han, Yongyun Qin, Xianqing Wang

item.title: The Cartan determinant conjecture for representation-finite Artin algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.14638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every representation-finite Artin algebra of finite global dimension has integral Cartan determinant one.
item.dc:creator: Liang Chen, Qianqian Guo

item.title: Extensions of locally analytic generalized Steinberg representations
item.description: arXiv:2211.00476v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\mathrm{Q}_p$. We study locally $\mathrm{Q}_p$-analytic generalized Steinberg representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ associated with a general Zelevinsky segment and compute certain $\mathrm{Ext}^1$-groups involving these representations. These extension groups give rise to parabolic Breuil simple $\mathcal{L}$-invariants on the automorphic side of a conjectural $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for potentially semistable $p$-adic Galois representations in the non-trianguline case.
item.dc:creator: Yiqin He

item.title: Parabolic Simple $\mathscr{L}$-Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2211.10847v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Let $\rho_L$ be a potentially semi-stable non-crystalline $p$-adic Galois representation such that the associated $F$-semisimple Weil-Deligne representation is absolutely indecomposable. In this paper, we study Fontaine-Mazur parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants of $\rho_L$, which was previously only known in the trianguline case. Based on the previous work on Breuil's parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants, we attach to $\rho_L$ a locally $\mathbf{Q}_p$-analytic representation $\Pi(\rho_L)$ of $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(L)$, which carries the information of parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants of $\rho_L$. When $\rho_L$ comes from a patched automorphic representation of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A}_{F^+})$ (for a define unitary group $\mathbf{G}$ over a totally real field $F^+$ which is compact at infinite places and $\mathrm{GL}_n$ at $p$-adic places), we prove under mild hypothesis that $\Pi(\rho_L)$ is a subrepresentation of the associated Hecke-isotypic subspace of the Banach spaces of (patched) $p$-adic automophic forms on $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A}_{F^+})$, this is equivalent to say that the Breuil's parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants are equal to Fontaine-Mazur parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants.
item.dc:creator: Yiqin He

item.title: Discrete $N$-particle systems at high temperature through Jack generating functions
item.description: arXiv:2502.13098v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find necessary and sufficient conditions for the Law of Large Numbers for random discrete $N$-particle systems with the deformation (inverse temperature) parameter $\theta$, as their size $N$ tends to infinity simultaneously with the inverse temperature going to zero. Our conditions are expressed in terms of the Jack generating functions, and our analysis is based on the asymptotics of the action of Cherednik operators obtained via Hecke relations. We apply the general framework to obtain the LLN for a large class of Markov chains of $N$ nonintersecting particles with interaction of log-gas type, and the LLN for the multiplication of Jack polynomials, as the inverse temperature tends to zero. We express the answer in terms of novel one-parameter deformations of cumulants and their description provided by us recovers previous work by Bufetov--Gorin [Geom. Funct. Anal. 25 (2015), no. 3, 763-814] on quantized free cumulants when $\theta=1$, and by Benaych-Georges--Cuenca--Gorin [Comm. Math. Phys. 394 (2022), no. 2, 735-795] after a deformation to continuous space of random matrix eigenvalues. Our methods are robust enough to be applied to the fixed temperature regime, where we recover the LLN of Huang [Adv. Math. 380 (2021), Paper No. 107545, 91].
item.dc:creator: Cesar Cuenca, Maciej Do{\l}\k{e}ga

item.title: Any-Dimensional Polynomial Optimization via de Finetti Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2507.15632v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polynomial optimization problems often arise in sequences indexed by dimension, and it is of interest to compute bounds on the optimal values of all problems in the sequence. Examples include certifying inequalities between symmetric functions or graph homomorphism densities that hold over vectors and graphs of all sizes, and computing the value of mean-field games viewed as limits of games with a growing number of players. In this paper, we study such any-dimensional polynomial problems using the theory of representation stability, and we develop a systematic framework to produce hierarchies of improving bounds on their limiting optimal values. Our bounds are obtained by solving finite-dimensional polynomial optimization problems (or their relaxations). These bounds converge at explicit rates as a consequence of new de Finetti-type theorems pertaining to sequences of random arrays projecting onto each other in different ways. The proofs of these theorems are based on applying results from probability to representations of certain categories. We apply our framework to produce new bounds on problems arising in a number of application domains such as mean-field games, extremal graph theory, and symmetric function theory, and we illustrate our methods via numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Eitan Levin, Venkat Chandrasekaran

item.title: Reconstruction of tensor categories of type $G_2$
item.description: arXiv:2510.09922v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that any ribbon tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with the fusion rules of the compact group of type $G_2$ is equivalent to the representation category of the corresponding Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group for $q^2=1$ or $q^2$ not a root of unity. We also prove an analogous result for the corresponding ribbon fusion tensor categories at roots of unity.
item.dc:creator: Lilit Martirosyan, Hans Wenzl

item.title: A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain
item.description: arXiv:2511.01245v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a Markov chain with very different mixing rates depending on how mixing is measured. The chain is the "Burnside process on the hypercube $C_2^n$." Started at the all-zeros state, it mixes in a bounded number of steps, no matter how large $n$ is, in $\ell^1$ and in $\ell^2$. And started at general $x$, it mixes in at most $\log n$ steps in $\ell^1$. But, in $\ell^2$, it takes $\frac{n}{\log n}$ steps for most starting $x$. The $\ell^2$ mixing results follow from an explicit diagonalization of the Markov chain into binomial-coefficient-valued eigenvectors.
item.dc:creator: Persi Diaconis, Andrew Lin, Arun Ram

item.title: GKLO representations for shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs
item.description: arXiv:2603.07250v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this note, we introduce shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs of split simply-laced type, and construct their GKLO representations, following similar recent developments in the case of shifted twisted Yangians. A full proof that our formulas yield a representation is given.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki

item.title: Arithmetic volume of Shtukas and Langlands duality
item.description: arXiv:2604.03763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the work of Feng--Yun--Zhang relating the arithmetic volume of Shtukas with derivatives of zeta functions by allowing arbitrary coweights for split semisimple algebraic groups. As in their original work, the formula involves some numbers called eigenweights. We obtain uniform formulas for the eigenweights in terms of the Langlands dual group, marking the first structural role for the dual group in such formulas governing derivatives of L-functions.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Wang, Wenqing Wei

item.title: Equivalence of categories of bivariant K-theory for C*-algebras over topological spaces via reflection functors
item.description: arXiv:2608.22317v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, for various pairs of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, we introduce an analogue of the Bern\v{s}te\u{\i}n-Gel'fand-Ponomarev reflection functors between the categories of C*-algebras over $X$ and $Y$. We prove that these functors induce equivalences $\mathfrak{KK}(X)_{\mathrm{loc}} \simeq \mathfrak{KK}(Y)_{\mathrm{loc}}$ between Meyer and Nest's localizing subcategories in Kirchberg's ideal-related KK-theory, and $\mathfrak{E}(X) \simeq \mathfrak{E}(Y)$ between the entire categories in Dadarlat and Meyer's ideal-related E-theory. Both equivalences restrict to the respective bootstrap categories: $\mathcal{B}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}(Y)$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(Y)$. Combining these equivalences with a combinatorial argument in quiver representation theory, we obtain the same equivalences for any two finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of the same tree. Moreover, we prove a rearrangement property of reflection functors, which yields an analogue of Coxeter functors. Finally, we apply reflection functors to give a conceptual alternative proof of Bentmann and K\"ohler's universal coefficient theorem for filtrated K-theory over finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of Dynkin diagrams of type A.
item.dc:creator: Nanami Hashimoto

item.title: Iterative construction of the R-matrices in arbitrary dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.06274v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a special ansats that allows for an iterative solution of the constant Yang-Baxter equation. Testing this ansatz, we construct four sequences of the constant R-matrices. In each sequence the R-matrices act on the tensor squares of vector spaces of linearly growing dimensions. Each R-matrix also depends on a single complex parameter. By analyzing the spectra of the R-matrices, we conclude that the first and the third series are associated with the symmetric tensor representations of the quantum groups U_q(sl(2)) and U_q(sl(2|1)), respectively. The other two series appear to be related to representations of quantum groups in the case where q is a root of unity. The elements of the second series are associated with nilpotent representations of U_q(sl(2)). We also check the correspondence between these R-matrices and link invariants. Applying the Reshetikhin-Turaev procedure to the first, second, and fourth sequences yields, respectively, colored Jones polynomials, ADO invariants, and Alexander polynomials. To our surprise, a similar calculation for the third series yields a trivial result, identically equal to 1.
item.dc:creator: Petr Pivovarov, Pavel Pyatov

item.title: Chow Vanishing and Motives of Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2609.19744v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the integral Chow groups $CH_i$ and mixed Hodge degree $H^{2i, (i, i)}$ cohomology groups of a really full rank (RFR) sink-recurrent cluster variety vanish for $i > 0$. In particular this applies to braid varieties and open projected Richardson varieties in any Lie type. Our main technical tool is the construction of a stratification of any RFR sink-recurrent cluster variety $\mathcal{A}(\Sigma)$ over any field $k$ into (affine space times) RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties of seeds with fewer mutable vertices than $\Sigma$, with which we show that RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties are linear in the sense of Totaro. We also show that cycle class maps are isomorphisms onto the lowest-weight part of rational Borel-Moore homology for any mixed Tate variety over a number field. Finally, we use our results to deduce vanishing theorems for the Khovanov-Rozansky homology groups of closures of positive braids and generation properties for the Chow groups of flag Richardson, projected Richardson, and brick varieties: namely, that these groups are generated integrally by the fundamental classes of their closed Richardson, positroid, and braid strata, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: Moments and Large Geometric Monodromy for Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.04099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$, and $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ for a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $\mathbb F_p$. For $n\ge2$ we study $\Sigma_n(h)=\sum_{u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n,\sum_i h_i u_i=-\lambda}\psi_q(\sum_i u_i^{-1})$. On $\mathbb G_m^n$ we construct a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$, pure of weight $n+1$ and rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, whose Frobenius traces equal $(-1)^{n-1}q\Sigma_n(h)$ minus an explicit polynomial in $q$, for $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$. For odd $p$, its geometric monodromy has identity component $\mathrm{SL}_{r(n)}$ and cyclic component group of order divisible by $p$. The full group is $\{g:\det(g)^p=1\}$ for $n=2$, and for $n\ge3$ using boundary unipotence from the companion preprint arXiv:2610.03081. For $p=2$, the sheaf is self-dual and its geometric monodromy is $\mathrm{SO}_{r(n)}$ for odd $n$ and $\mathrm{Sp}_{r(n)}$ for even $n$. After normalization to weight zero, the arithmetic and geometric groups coincide, using the same companion input for odd $p$ and $n\ge3$. As $q\to\infty$ with $p$ fixed, we obtain Sato-Tate laws for centered, normalized sums with error $O(q^{-1/2})$ for polynomial tests and formulas for all power moments. For $p=2$, limiting moments are Gaussian through order $r(n)-1$, with an excess of one above the orthogonal value at order $r(n)$ for odd $n$; if $n+1$ is a power of two, every Frobenius on $\mathcal W_n$ has eigenvalue $q^{(n+1)/2}$. The proof uses $\sum_h|\Sigma_n(h)|^4=c_pq^{3n-2}+O(q^{3n-2-\delta(n)})$ for $n\ge3$, where $c_p=2$ for odd $p$, $c_2=3$ and $\delta(n)=\min(1,(n-2)/2)$, plane sections of the Cayley cubic, exact Frobenius-Schur identities, Laumon's local Fourier transforms and Artin-Schreier theory. For $n=2$ we identify twisted classical Kloosterman sums and compute the fourth moment exactly.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: On the number of cokernel-closed additive subcategories for uniformly oriented $A_n$ quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.07999v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the integer sequence that enumerates cokernel-closed, idempotent split, full, additive subcategories of the category of finite dimensional complex representations of a uniformly oriented $A_n$ quiver. Using a combinatorial model, we describe a non-obvious connection of this sequence to Catalan numbers and derive an implicit recurrence. We also describe some basic properties of the lattice underlying the sequences, in particular, we give an explicit description of the meet irreducible elements of that lattice.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Mazorchuk, Shuoyang Xu

item.title: Local Constancy of the Betti Automorphic Category over the Moduli of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.12384v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nadler and Yun conjectured that the automorphic side of the Betti geometric Langlands correspondence forms a local system of categories over the moduli of curves. We prove this local constancy conjecture using purely microlocal methods, independent of the recently established Betti geometric Langlands conjecture. In particular, it follows that the Betti automorphic category depends only on the genus of the curve, verifying a conjecture of Ben-Zvi and Nadler.
item.dc:creator: Joakim F{\ae}rgeman, Marius Kj{\ae}rsgaard
